promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: The work of designers and design movements

questions.q: What does the term 'anthropometrics' mean?
options: The measurement of the sizes and proportions of the human body
The study of how colour affects a product's appeal
The testing of a material's strength and durability
The process of recycling products at end of life
questions.explain: Anthropometrics is the collection and use of data on human body measurements to inform design.

questions.q: Ergonomics is best described as the study of the relationship between people and:
options: The products, systems and environments they use
The historical periods of design movements
The cost of manufacturing a product
questions.explain: Ergonomics considers how people interact with products and environments to improve comfort, safety and efficiency.

questions.q: Which percentile represents the average value in a set of anthropometric data?
questions.explain: The 50th percentile is the midpoint of the data, representing the average-sized user.

questions.q: Why do designers commonly use the range from the 5th to the 95th percentile?
options: It accommodates about 90% of the intended user population
It includes every possible user without exception
It only considers the smallest 5% of users
It represents the exact average of all users
questions.explain: Designing between the 5th and 95th percentiles covers roughly 90% of users while excluding costly extremes.

questions.q: A designer is deciding the height of a doorway so that almost all users can pass through without stooping. Which percentile should the height be based on?
questions.explain: Clearance dimensions such as doorway height are set to the tallest users (95th percentile) so shorter users are also accommodated.

questions.q: Applying good ergonomics to a product mainly improves which of the following?
options: The rarity of the materials used
questions.explain: Ergonomic design aims to make products comfortable, safe and efficient for people to use.

questions.q: A designer wants an office chair to suit users of many different sizes. What is the most appropriate approach?
options: Make the seat height and back adjustable across a range of percentiles
Design it only for the 50th percentile user
Design it only for the 95th percentile user
Ignore anthropometric data and use a fixed standard size
questions.explain: Adjustability lets one chair fit a wide range of users, typically from the 5th to the 95th percentile.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the '6 Rs' of sustainability?
questions.explain: The 6 Rs commonly include Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, Refuse, Rethink and Repair.

questions.q: In the '6 Rs', what does 'Reduce' encourage a designer to do?
options: Use fewer materials and less energy to make a product
Add more decorative features to a product
Increase the size of the packaging
questions.explain: Reduce means minimising the resources and energy used, cutting waste and environmental impact.

questions.q: A life cycle assessment (LCA) analyses a product's environmental impact from:
options: Raw material extraction through to disposal ('cradle to grave')
The moment it is bought until it is sold
questions.explain: An LCA evaluates impacts across the whole life of a product, from raw materials to end-of-life disposal.

questions.q: A material described as 'biodegradable' will:
options: Break down naturally through the action of micro-organisms
Never decompose once it is discarded
Only decompose if it is burned
questions.explain: Biodegradable materials decompose naturally through microbial action, reducing long-term waste.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a renewable resource?
questions.explain: Timber is renewable because forests can be replanted, unlike finite fossil fuels and ores.

questions.q: A product's 'carbon footprint' refers to:
options: The total greenhouse gases produced across its life
The physical size of the product's base
The number of parts the product contains
The weight of the product's packaging
questions.explain: Carbon footprint measures the greenhouse gas emissions linked to making, using and disposing of a product.

questions.q: A manufacturer wants to lower the environmental impact of a metal casing. Which choice best supports sustainability?
options: Use recycled aluminium instead of newly mined aluminium
Use more raw material than needed for a heavier feel
Choose a finish that prevents the metal being recycled later
Ship components by air rather than sea to save no time
questions.explain: Recycled aluminium uses far less energy than extracting new metal, reducing environmental impact.

questions.q: Who founded the Bauhaus design school?
questions.explain: The Bauhaus was founded by the architect Walter Gropius in Germany.

questions.q: In which year was the Bauhaus school founded?
questions.explain: The Bauhaus was established in Weimar, Germany, in 1919.

questions.q: The principle 'form follows function' suggests that a product's shape should be determined mainly by its:
options: Intended purpose and how it will be used
questions.explain: 'Form follows function' means the appearance of an object should be driven by its intended use.

questions.q: The Memphis Group, known for bold colours and playful, geometric designs in the 1980s, was led by:
questions.explain: The Memphis Group was founded in Milan and led by the designer Ettore Sottsass.

questions.q: William Morris is most closely associated with which movement, which valued traditional craftsmanship over mass production?
questions.explain: William Morris was a leading figure of the Arts and Crafts movement, championing hand craftsmanship.

questions.q: A product features bold geometric shapes, symmetry and sleek streamlined forms typical of the 1920s and 1930s. Which movement does it most reflect?
questions.explain: Art Deco of the 1920s-30s is characterised by bold geometric shapes, symmetry and streamlined, luxurious forms.
